creators.name: Aisha Al Mansoori
creators.bio: Weekend explorer. Desert sunrises, souk snacks, zero fuss.

creators.name: Rohan Mathew
creators.bio: Malayali in Abu Dhabi. A road trip every long weekend.

creators.name: Sara Thomas
creators.bio: Nurse by day, planner of very cheap trips by night.

creators.name: Omar Haddad
creators.bio: Hikes, wadis and anything with a view.

creators.name: Lena Fischer
creators.bio: German in the Gulf. Culture, coffee and long walks.

journeys.title: 48 Hours in Old Dubai on AED 900
journeys.dek: Abra rides for a dirham, the souks, the Creek at sunset and the world’s tallest building — without the price tag.
journeys.pullQuote: The best ride in Dubai costs one dirham and comes with a view of the Creek.
journeys.story: Everyone thinks Dubai is expensive. The old side isn’t. We stayed in Deira, ate where the taxi drivers eat, and spent our money on one splurge: the view from the top.

fields.label: Getting around
fields.value: Metro + abra; a Nol card covers both

stops.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
stops.story: Wind towers, coral-stone walls and quiet lanes — Dubai before the skyline. The coffee museum is worth the entry.
stops.tip: Go before 10 am; after that the alleys are an oven.

stops.name: Dubai Creek Abra
stops.story: The wooden abra crosses the Creek in five minutes for one dirham. We went back and forth three times just for the view.
stops.tip: Keep coins ready; the boatman collects mid-crossing.

stops.name: Gold Souk & Spice Souk
stops.story: Window-shopping at the Gold Souk, then the Spice Souk next door, where we actually spent — saffron, dried limes, frankincense.
stops.tip: Bargain: start at half the first price.

stops.name: Burj Khalifa & Dubai Fountain
stops.story: The fountain show every 30 minutes is free. We saved our splurge for At the Top at sunset.
stops.tip: Book At the Top online — it’s cheaper than at the counter.

stops.name: JBR Beach
stops.story: A free public beach with showers. We ended with our toes in the water and the giant wheel lighting up.
stops.tip: Sunset is busy; walk south for quieter sand.

journeys.title: Abu Dhabi, Slowly
journeys.dek: Two unhurried days between the Grand Mosque at golden hour, the Louvre’s rain of light and a sunset ride on the Corniche.
journeys.pullQuote: Under the Louvre’s dome the light falls like rain through palm leaves. I sat there for an hour.
journeys.story: Abu Dhabi rewards slowness. Most of the best things here are free or close to it, the buses are good, and nobody hurries you.

fields.label: Dress code
fields.value: Modest clothing for the mosque; abayas lent free

stops.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
stops.story: Free entry, booked online. Go for the last hour of daylight: the white marble turns gold, then blue.
stops.tip: Book the free slot a day ahead; walk-ins wait.

stops.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
stops.story: The building is the exhibit: a floating dome that throws spots of light everywhere. The galleries walk you through world history in one loop.

stops.name: Qasr Al Watan
stops.story: The presidential palace is open to visitors and absurdly grand — the library alone is worth it.

stops.name: Abu Dhabi Corniche
stops.story: Eight kilometres of promenade. Rent a bike, stop at the public beach, finish at the breakwater for sunset.
stops.tip: Bike docks every few hundred metres.

journeys.title: Jebel Jais: The UAE’s Rooftop
journeys.dek: Zipline the world’s longest, sleep in the mountains at 1,900 m, and drive the hairpins down to a sea-front fort at dawn.
journeys.pullQuote: At the top of Jebel Jais it was 14°C. Dubai, ninety minutes away, was 34.
journeys.story: Ras Al Khaimah is the UAE’s surprise. Ninety minutes from Dubai you climb a road of hairpins into cool air, eagles and silence.

fields.label: Temperature
fields.value: 10–15°C cooler than the coast; bring a jacket

stops.name: Jebel Jais Viewing Deck
stops.story: Pull over at the viewing deck for the first look down the wadis. The wind up here is serious.

stops.name: Jais Flight Zipline
stops.story: Nearly 3 km at up to 150 km/h, face-down like a falcon. Terrifying for ten seconds, then the best two minutes of the trip.
stops.tip: Weekends sell out — book a week ahead.

stops.name: Mountain cabin, Jebel Jais
stops.story: We slept in a cabin up the mountain and cooked over a fire. Stars like you never see in the city.

stops.name: Dhayah Fort
stops.story: A short, steep climb to a mud-brick fort over palm groves and the sea. Go at sunrise on the way down.

stops.name: Al Marjan Island
stops.story: Breakfast with our feet in the sand before the drive home.

journeys.title: Hatta for Under AED 400
journeys.dek: Turquoise dam water, a kayak, a bike trail and a village from the 1800s — on a nurse’s budget.
journeys.pullQuote: The dam is the colour of a cartoon swimming pool, surrounded by bare brown mountains.
journeys.story: We left Sharjah at 6, were kayaking by 8 and home for dinner. Hatta is the easiest mountain escape in the UAE.

fields.label: Bring
fields.value: Water shoes, sunscreen, cash for the honey stalls

stops.name: Hatta Dam
stops.story: Rent a kayak or a pedal boat. The water is impossibly turquoise against the Hajar mountains.
stops.tip: Kayaks run out by 10 am on Fridays.

stops.name: Hatta Wadi Hub
stops.story: Trails, a zipline and a giant slide down the hill. We did the easy bike loop and called it a workout.

stops.name: Hatta Heritage Village
stops.story: Mud-brick houses, a falaj water channel and watchtowers. Free, and almost empty on a weekday.

stops.name: Hatta Honey Bee Garden
stops.story: Taste local honeys straight from the comb; the sidr honey is liquid gold.

journeys.title: A Night in the Empty Quarter
journeys.dek: Moreeb Dune at sunset, a tent among red sand, and the silence of the Rub’ al Khali.
journeys.pullQuote: There is no sound in the Empty Quarter at night. We could hear each other blink.
journeys.story: Liwa is four hours from Dubai and feels like another planet. These are the tallest dunes in the country — orange at dawn, red at dusk.

fields.label: Car
fields.value: A normal car is fine on the roads; never drive on sand without a 4x4

stops.name: Liwa Oasis
stops.story: A crescent of date farms along the edge of the dunes. Stop at a roadside stall for fresh dates and coffee.

stops.name: Moreeb Dune
stops.story: Three hundred metres of sand rising like a wall. We climbed halfway and watched the sunset from there.

stops.name: Qasr Al Sarab
stops.story: We couldn’t afford a night at the palace resort, so we camped nearby and came here for one very fancy dinner.

stops.name: Mezaira’a
stops.story: Breakfast in the main town and a slow drive home through the dunes.

journeys.title: The East Coast: Snoopy Island & Khor Fakkan
journeys.dek: Snorkelling with turtles, the UAE’s oldest mosque, and a corniche where the mountains meet the sea.
journeys.pullQuote: Snorkelling off Snoopy Island, a turtle swam past my daughter’s mask. She hasn’t stopped talking about it.
journeys.story: Our family’s favourite long weekend. The east coast has mountains running straight into a calm sea, at half the price of the west.

fields.label: Kids
fields.value: Calm, shallow water — great for children

stops.name: Al Bidya Mosque
stops.story: The oldest mosque in the UAE: small, mud-walled, with watchtowers on the hill behind.

stops.name: Snoopy Island
stops.story: Rent snorkel gear on the beach and swim out — reef fish, sometimes turtles and baby sharks.
stops.tip: Go early; the water is clearest before noon.

stops.name: Fujairah Fort
stops.story: A centuries-old fort being restored, with a small heritage village next door.

stops.name: Khor Fakkan Beach
stops.story: A long corniche with mountains behind it. The new waterfall park is free and the kids ran around until sunset.

journeys.title: Musandam: Arabia’s Fjords by Dhow
journeys.dek: A wooden dhow through mountain fjords, dolphins off the bow, and a swim at Telegraph Island.
journeys.pullQuote: Dolphins raced the dhow for ten minutes. Nobody on board said a word.
journeys.story: Musandam is Oman’s northern tip, wrapped around the Strait of Hormuz. Cross the border at Tibat and you’re among cliffs plunging into blue water.

fields.label: Border
fields.value: Oman border visa — check your passport

stops.name: Khasab
stops.story: A sleepy port town; the harbour full of dhows is the real sight.

stops.name: Khor Ash Sham
stops.story: The longest fjord. Our dhow cruised it for hours, past fishing villages you can only reach by boat.

stops.name: Telegraph Island
stops.story: A tiny island with the ruins of an 1860s British telegraph station. We jumped off the dhow and swam around it.

stops.name: Khasab Castle
stops.story: A 17th-century fort with a good little museum, then seafood by the water.

journeys.title: Muscat & Wadi Shab on a Shoestring
journeys.dek: Swim through a cave to a hidden waterfall, wander Mutrah Souq, and stare into the Bimmah Sinkhole.
journeys.pullQuote: To reach the waterfall in Wadi Shab you swim through a gap in the rock barely wider than your head.
journeys.story: We flew Sharjah–Muscat on a budget airline and rented the smallest car available. Oman is cheaper than it looks if you eat local and sleep simple.

fields.label: Visa
fields.value: eVisa or visa-free for many — check before booking

stops.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
stops.story: One of the largest chandeliers in the world, over a hand-woven carpet the size of a football pitch.

stops.name: Mutrah Souq
stops.story: Frankincense smoke, silver khanjars and the best halwa we’ve had. Walk the corniche to the fort at dusk.

stops.name: Bimmah Sinkhole
stops.story: A turquoise pool inside a collapsed limestone cave, with tiny fish that nibble your toes.

stops.name: Wadi Shab
stops.story: A short boat across, a 45-minute hike, then swim through pools to the cave with the waterfall inside.
stops.tip: Waterproof phone pouch — you will be swimming.

stops.name: Ras al Jinz
stops.story: Green turtles come ashore to nest at night. Watching a hatchling run for the sea is something we’ll never forget.

journeys.title: Tbilisi & Kazbegi in Five Days
journeys.dek: Sulphur baths, khachapuri for breakfast, and a ride up to a church in the clouds below Mount Kazbek.
journeys.pullQuote: From the Gergeti church you look across at a glacier, and the only sound is cowbells.
journeys.story: Georgia is the Gulf’s favourite cool-weather escape: under four hours’ flight, wine country, and mountains you can reach in a morning.

fields.label: Visa
fields.value: Visa-free for many UAE residents — check yours

stops.name: Old Tbilisi
stops.story: Wooden balconies, the domes of the sulphur baths and a cable car up to Narikala fortress.

stops.name: Fabrika
stops.story: A Soviet sewing factory turned courtyard of cafés. Our favourite place to eat cheap.

stops.name: Ananuri Fortress
stops.story: A fortress-church on a turquoise reservoir, on the drive north along the old Military Road.

stops.name: Gergeti Trinity Church
stops.story: The famous church at 2,170 m. We took a 4x4 up and hiked down through the meadows.

stops.name: Gudauri
stops.story: We paraglided over the valleys — twenty minutes of floating above the Caucasus.

journeys.title: Monsoon in Munnar
journeys.dek: Tea hills in the clouds, a boat on Mattupetty and a sunrise above the mist — a long weekend home from Abu Dhabi.
journeys.pullQuote: In July the fog pours over the tea bushes like milk into a glass.
journeys.story: We fly home to Kerala every summer. This time we stole three days in the hills before the family found us.

fields.label: Getting there
fields.value: Fly to Kochi, then 4 hours by road

fields.label: Monsoon
fields.value: Check road conditions before driving up

stops.name: Munnar
stops.story: The last hour of the drive is all hairpins and tea, the bushes clipped so evenly they look like green coral.

stops.name: Mattupetty Dam
stops.story: A pedal boat on the reservoir in the mist — completely silent except for the rain.

stops.name: Top Station
stops.story: We left at 5 am and waited. At 7:10 the clouds tore open and we were standing above a sea of white.

credit.author: Bimal K C from Cochin, India

stops.name: Vattavada
stops.story: Terraced vegetable farms up the slopes. A farmer sold us strawberries by the kilo.

credit.author: Bimal K C from Cochin, India
